question: What is the primary medical reason for inserting a cardiac pacemaker?
explanation: Pacemakers are primarily inserted to correct slow heart rhythms that fail to maintain adequate cardiac output. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h1)

question: The insulated wires connecting the pulse generator to the heart are called what?
explanation: Leads transmit electrical impulses from the pulse generator directly to the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h1)

question: A pacemaker with leads placed in both the right atrium and right ventricle is known as what?
explanation: Using two leads allows the device to pace and sense in both the atrium and the ventricle. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: How do rate-responsive pacemakers adjust pacing speed during physical exertion?

options.A: Sensing nervous system signals from the brain
options.B: Detecting physical movement via built-in sensors
options.C: Measuring direct oxygen saturation in the blood
options.D: Calculating body temperature changes in the skin

explanation: Special sensors in the generator pick up physical activity and speed up the heart rate accordingly. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: Why is the chest hair clipped instead of shaved prior to pacemaker insertion?

options.B: To reduce patient discomfort from itching
options.C: To speed up the skin preparation process
options.D: To ensure better adhesive pad contact

explanation: Shaving causes tiny cuts on the skin that can harbor bacteria and increase the risk of surgical site infection. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: A patient scheduled for pacemaker insertion asks why fasting is required. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: To ensure accurate blood glucose readings throughout the day
options.B: To prevent electrolyte imbalances during the surgical procedure
options.C: To reduce the risk of vomiting and aspiration during sedation
options.D: To keep the gastrointestinal tract completely empty for imaging

explanation: Fasting protects the airway by minimizing stomach contents when sedatives or local anesthetics are administered. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: What diagnostic imaging is routinely performed immediately after pacemaker insertion?
explanation: A chest X-ray checks lead position and confirms the absence of a collapsed lung. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h4)

question: A patient who just returned from pacemaker insertion tries to reach for a cup on a high shelf. What immediate action should the nurse take?

options.A: Instruct the patient to lower the arm and avoid raising it above the shoulder
options.B: Administer a dose of prescribed analgesics to manage expected surgical pain
options.C: Check the underlying heart rhythm on the bedside telemetry monitor
options.D: Apply a firm sandbag directly over the surgical wound dressing

explanation: Raising the arm too high can dislodge the fresh leads from the heart tissue. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h4)

question: What weight lifting limit is typically advised for the affected arm after pacemaker insertion?
explanation: Limiting lifting to about five kilograms prevents undue tension on the healing tissue and leads. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which instruction is correct regarding hygiene for a new pacemaker incision site?

options.A: Soak the chest area in warm water to loosen dried blood
options.B: Apply medicated petroleum jelly directly over the staples daily
options.C: Keep the wound dry until healthcare providers remove the dressing
options.D: Scrub the incision daily with antibacterial soap during a bath

explanation: Keeping the incision dry prevents bacteria from entering the surgical pocket before the skin seals. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h5)

question: What electrocardiogram finding defines pacemaker failure to capture?

options.A: Pacing spikes occurring too close to the T wave
options.B: Continuous rapid firing exceeding normal limits
options.C: Pacing spikes present without following QRS complexes
options.D: Complete absence of any electrical pacing spikes

explanation: Failure to capture means the electrical stimulus was delivered but failed to depolarize the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h6)

question: A patient with a temporary pacemaker becomes dizzy, and telemetry shows spikes not synchronized with the intrinsic beats. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Increase the generator output settings to maximum voltage
options.B: Assess vital signs and notify the attending physician immediately
options.C: Turn the patient onto the left side and administer oxygen
options.D: Disconnect the external battery source for thirty seconds

explanation: Hemodynamic instability requires immediate clinical assessment and physician intervention to adjust the device. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h6)

question: What document should a pacemaker patient carry to show security personnel during travel?
explanation: The card confirms the presence of an implanted medical device and helps bypass electronic security systems. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why should patients with pacemakers avoid undergoing standard magnetic resonance imaging scans?

options.A: Imaging signals permanently erase all programmed patient history
options.B: Strong magnetic fields can disrupt device function and heat the leads
options.C: Radio waves completely drain the internal battery within seconds
options.D: The metallic casing causes severe distortion on the scan images

explanation: Powerful magnets in MRI machines can reprogram the device or cause thermal injury to heart tissue via the leads. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the purpose of remote monitoring for patients with cardiac pacemakers?

options.A: To transmit device data and check function from home
options.B: To track physical exercise and step counts in real time
options.C: To provide live video consultation with the surgeon
options.D: To automatically adjust medication dosages daily

explanation: Remote monitoring allows clinicians to evaluate device performance and battery status without requiring clinic visits. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)

question: A patient expresses intense anxiety about the pacemaker battery running out unexpectedly. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Explain that devices provide gradual warning signs well before battery depletion
options.B: Assure the patient that the current battery will last forever without replacement
options.C: Recommend immediate surgical replacement of the pulse generator today
options.D: Tell the patient to avoid all physical activity to save remaining battery power

explanation: Batteries degrade slowly and regular checks catch declining power levels long before failure occurs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)
